ideas.title: Add default OG / Twitter card image across all pages
ideas.problem: Every page — home, section indexes, and detail pages — is missing `og:image` and `twitter:card` image. When shared on social platforms (X/Twitter, LinkedIn, Slack), no preview image is shown; Twitter falls back to `summary` card (text only) with no visual. This directly reduces click-through on social shares.
ideas.proposal: Create a single 1200×630 px fallback OG image (e.g. `public/og-default.png`) and add `<meta property="og:image">` / `<meta name="twitter:image">` to `BaseLayout.astro`. Accept an optional `image` prop (defaulting to the fallback) so `SectionEntryLayout` can generate page-specific images in the future. Also upgrade `twitter:card` from `summary` to `summary_large_image` once an image is present.
ideas.evidence: dist/index.html: no `og:image` or `twitter:image` tag in `<head>`. dist/concepts/what-is-an-agent/index.html: same. public/ directory contains only `ads.txt` and `robots.txt` — no image assets of any kind. src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro line 34: `<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary">` (no image tag follows).
open_questions: Should per-page OG images be generated at build time (e.g. via @vercel/og or satori), or is a single static fallback sufficient for now?
What branding elements should appear on the OG image (title, site name, accent color)?
ideas.mockup_hint: code diff — before/after showing added og:image and twitter:image meta tags in BaseLayout.astro, plus upgrade twitter:card to summary_large_image

ideas.title: Add Cache-Control: immutable for content-hashed static assets
ideas.problem: The `/_astro/` directory contains content-hashed JS and CSS files (e.g. `/_astro/about.R4vga0ua.css`, `/_astro/hoisted.BeUxVHN1.js`). Vercel's default Cache-Control for these is short-lived. Without `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, repeat visitors re-download identical bytes every visit, wasting bandwidth and slowing repeat-page loads.
ideas.proposal: Add a second `headers` rule in `vercel.json` targeting `/_astro/(.*)` (and optionally `/pagefind/(.*)`) with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. The content-hash in the filename guarantees cache-busting on every build, so the long TTL is safe.
ideas.evidence: vercel.json lines 6–16: single `headers` block matching `/(.*)`; contains four security headers but no `Cache-Control`. dist/_astro/ contains `about.R4vga0ua.css` (22 KB) and `hoisted.BeUxVHN1.js` (5.4 KB) — both have content hashes and should be immutably cached.
open_questions: Should /pagefind/ assets also get immutable headers? They are regenerated each build but not content-hashed by filename.
ideas.mockup_hint: code diff — before/after vercel.json showing the new /_astro/(.*) header rule

ideas.title: Non-blocking Google Fonts loading to improve FCP / LCP
ideas.problem: The Google Fonts `<link rel="stylesheet">` in `BaseLayout.astro` is synchronous and render-blocking. The browser must fetch and parse the external CSS before painting any text, which delays First Contentful Paint and Largest Contentful Paint on every page load. `display=swap` is set on the font URL but the CSS request itself still blocks rendering.
ideas.proposal: Replace the synchronous `<link rel="stylesheet">` with the standard async-load pattern: `<link rel="preload" as="style" onload="this.rel='stylesheet'">` plus a `<noscript>` fallback. The existing `<link rel="preconnect">` tags can stay. This makes the font CSS non-blocking: text renders immediately in the fallback stack, then swaps to Fraunces/Inter/JetBrains Mono once the font CSS arrives.
ideas.evidence: src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro line 39: `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...&display=swap" rel="stylesheet" />` — the `rel="stylesheet"` with no `media` trick or `preload` makes this request render-blocking. No `prefers-reduced-motion` guard needed here (font-loading is not an animation).
open_questions: Is self-hosting the fonts (via fontsource packages) preferred to reduce third-party DNS lookups entirely?
ideas.mockup_hint: code diff — before/after showing the link tag changed from rel=stylesheet to rel=preload as=style with onload swap and noscript fallback

ideas.title: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD to concept/deep-dive detail pages; add WebSite JSON-LD to home
ideas.problem: Concept and deep-dive detail pages emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD but omit `BreadcrumbList` structured data. Google Search uses `BreadcrumbList` to render breadcrumb trails in SERPs, which increases snippet real-estate and click-through. The home page emits no JSON-LD at all, missing a `WebSite` + `SearchAction` entity that enables the Google Sitelinks search box. Field-guide chapter pages also have zero JSON-LD.
ideas.proposal: In `SectionEntryLayout.astro`, extend the existing `jsonLd` constant into a `@graph` array that includes both the `TechArticle` node and a `BreadcrumbList` node (Section → Entry). In `HomeView.astro` (or `BaseLayout.astro`), inject a `WebSite` node with `potentialAction.SearchAction` pointing at the Pagefind query URL. In `ChapterLayout.astro`, add a `TechArticle` + `BreadcrumbList` node mirroring the pattern from `SectionEntryLayout`.
ideas.evidence: dist/concepts/what-is-an-agent/index.html JSON-LD: `{"@type":"TechArticle","headline":"What Is an AI Agent?","description":"...","inLanguage":"en","url":"..."}` — no `BreadcrumbList`, no `author`, no `datePublished`. dist/index.html: zero `application/ld+json` script tags. dist/field-guide/the-loop/index.html: zero `application/ld+json` script tags.
open_questions: The field-guide chapters don't have individual `datePublished` metadata — should we omit that field or use a placeholder?
Should `WebSite.SearchAction` use Pagefind's URL pattern or just omit it since search is client-side only?
ideas.mockup_hint: code diff — SectionEntryLayout.astro jsonLd before/after showing @graph with TechArticle + BreadcrumbList nodes

ideas.title: Add :focus-visible styles for header nav links, sidebar links, and locale switcher
ideas.problem: Keyboard users who tab through the site-header nav links, the section sidebar (`chapter-side-nav li a`), and the locale switcher (`lang-switch a`) receive only the browser's default focus ring. No custom `:focus-visible` rule exists for these elements in `site.css`. This is a WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.4.11 (Focus Appearance) gap and inconsistent with the existing custom focus treatment on `.site-search-trigger` and `.skip-link`.
ideas.proposal: Add `:focus-visible` rules for `.site-header nav a`, `.chapter-side-nav li a`, and `.lang-switch a` in `site.css` that apply `outline: 2px solid var(--accent)` (matching the skip-link pattern) or the inset `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--accent)` used on the search trigger. Remove any `outline: none` that suppresses the default ring without providing a replacement.
ideas.evidence: src/styles/site.css: `.site-header nav a` (lines 20–23) — hover rule at line 26 but no `:focus-visible` rule. `.chapter-side-nav li a` (lines 64–68) — hover at line 69 but no `:focus-visible` rule. `.lang-switch a` (lines 92–98) — hover at line 98 but no `:focus-visible` rule. Contrast: `.site-search-trigger:focus-visible` (line 148) has `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--accent)` — a proper custom focus indicator already exists there.
open_questions: Should the sidebar's active-item left-border accent double as a focus indicator, or should a separate outline be added?
ideas.mockup_hint: code diff — before/after site.css showing added :focus-visible rules for nav a, sidebar links, and lang-switch a

ideas.title: Respect prefers-reduced-motion for smooth-scroll and CSS transitions
ideas.problem: `guide.css` sets `html { scroll-behavior: smooth }` globally without a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` override. Four `transition: all 0.15s` rules in `guide.css` (lines 93, 146, 469, 639) and one in `site.css` (line 107) are also never guarded. Users who opt into reduced motion (vestibular disorders, motion sensitivity) get smooth-scrolling and animated transitions anyway, violating WCAG 2.1 SC 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions, AAA) and the practical expectation of the OS setting.
ideas.proposal: Add a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block at the bottom of `guide.css` (and/or `site.css`) that sets `html { scroll-behavior: auto }` and overrides all `transition` properties to `transition: none`. This is a one-block addition of ~8 lines; no component changes needed.
ideas.evidence: src/styles/guide.css line 24: `html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }` — no matching reduced-motion override. Lines 93, 146, 469, 639: `transition: all 0.15s;` — no reduced-motion guard. src/styles/site.css line 107: `transition: color .12s, border-bottom-color .12s;` — no guard. `grep -r prefers-reduced-motion src/` returns no results.
open_questions: Are there any JS-driven animations (e.g. in SiteSearch.astro) that also need a `matchMedia` check?
ideas.mockup_hint: code diff — guide.css addition of @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block covering scroll-behavior and transition overrides

ideas.title: Add Pagefind section filters (data-pagefind-filter) to scope search by content type
ideas.problem: The search index is a flat, undifferentiated corpus. There is no way for users to filter results to a specific section (Field Guide vs. Concepts vs. Deep-Dives). All `data-pagefind-filter` and `data-pagefind-meta` attributes are absent from the built HTML. This means a query like "tool use" returns a noisy mix of entries from all three content types with no way to narrow results.
ideas.proposal: Add `data-pagefind-filter="section:<SectionName>"` to the `<main>` (or `<article>`) element in each detail layout: `section:Field Guide` in `ChapterLayout.astro`, `section:Concepts` in `ConceptLayout.astro` (or `SectionEntryLayout`), and `section:Deep Dives` in `DeepDiveLayout.astro`. Then pass `filters: true` (or an explicit `filters` config) to the `PagefindUI` constructor in `SiteSearch.astro` so the filter UI is rendered. Section index pages and home can be tagged `section:Index` or excluded.
ideas.evidence: src/components/SiteSearch.astro lines 95–102: `PagefindUI` constructor has no `filters` key. `grep -r 'data-pagefind-filter' src/` returns no results. `grep -r 'data-pagefind-filter' dist/` also returns no results. The search corpus includes all 135 en content pages (field-guide, concepts, deep-dives) indexed together.
open_questions: Should the filter UI display section labels in both English and Chinese depending on locale?
Does Pagefind's language-scoped indexing (per html lang) interact with section filters — i.e. do EN and ZH pages need separate filter values?
ideas.mockup_hint: code diff — SectionEntryLayout.astro adding data-pagefind-filter to article element; SiteSearch.astro adding filters option to PagefindUI constructor

notes: No missing hreflang pairs were found: both inline `<link rel=alternate>` tags and the sitemap xhtml:link entries correctly cross-reference en and zh-Hans for all 135 bilingual page pairs. The lang attribute on zh pages is correctly `zh-Hans` (BaseLayout.astro line 18). Color contrast passes WCAG AA for all measured token pairs: muted (#6b6358) on paper (#f4f1ea) = 5.24:1, code-comment (#8a8270) on code-bg (#1a1a1a) = 4.56:1. No images exist in the current content so there are no missing loading=lazy or dimension attributes to fix. The sitemap covers all 270 pages (135 EN + 135 ZH) with no gaps. There is no favicon at all (no /favicon.ico, no <link rel=icon>) — this was not elevated to a top card because it is purely cosmetic / brand, not a Core Web Vitals or WCAG issue, but it should be added in a follow-up.
